item.title: Kepa Arrizabalaga admits Arsenal dressing room frustration after Borussia Dortmund Champions League draw despite stepping in for injured David Raya
item.description: Arsenal FC v Borussia Dortmund - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Kepa Arrizabalaga has opened up on the feeling of frustration inside the Arsenal dressing room following Tuesday's 1-1 Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund. The Spanish goalkeeper was called into action at the Emirates Stadium after David Raya was sidelined with a shoulder problem. Stepping into the spotlight Arsenal maintained their unbeaten status in European competition this season, but the mood in North London was far from celebratory after a stalemate against the German giants . Kepa , who earned his first continental start of the campaign, found himself between the posts as Mikel Arteta’s side looked to solidify their position in the top eight of the league phase. The opportunity arose following a late injury blow to first-choice keeper David Raya , who sustained a shoulder issue during the weekend's Premier League clash with Newcastle United. The former Chelsea man performed well under pressure, but he admitted that the squad felt they had let two points slip away against the current Bundesliga leaders. Despite the quality of the opposition, the Gunners were the more dominant force for large periods of the contest. "We are a bit disappointed with the result," said Kepa on the club's official website . "I think it's a game that we should win, we created enough chances. I think we played very well against a very strong side. Sometimes football is like this, but if we keep playing like this, if we keep creating chances like this, I think we are in a good way." Dealing with late drama The atmosphere at the Emirates was electric as the home fans pushed for a decisive goal in the closing stages of the match. Arsenal threw everything forward in search of a winner, but the Dortmund defence held firm to secure a share of the spoils. For Kepa, the failure to find that late breakthrough was the primary source of the post-match disappointment within the camp. "We wanted the win, we were playing in front of our fans. Until the end, we pushed, the atmosphere was brilliant, I think we were very close. And when you don’t get that late goal, you are a bit frustrated, but I think we have to take the positives. I think we played very well, they are first in the Bundesliga. They are a really good team and I think we played them in a good way," the 32-year-old goalkeeper continued. Ready for the call Stepping in for Raya required a quick mental shift for Kepa, who has spent much of the season providing cover. However, the Spaniard insisted he was prepared for the challenge and was pleased to have the chance to contribute to the team’s European journey. He noted the difference between this start and other emergency appearances he has had to make in the past. "At least today I had a warm-up to go out!” he smiled when discussing the late change in the starting lineup. "But yeah, happy to be out there, happy to help the team. item.title: C/River imposes curfew on Iso-Bendeghe, Boje over deadly land clashes
item.description: .bans entry into disputed areas, orders security agencies to enforce order By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Government has imposed an immediate dusk-to-dawn curfew on Iso-Bendeghe and Boje communities in Boki Local Government Area, following protracted clashes over a land dispute between the two neighbours. The curfew, announced Wednesday in a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Pst. Ekpenyong Cobham, will last one week from November 24, 2026. Cobham said the measure became necessary because the crisis was threatening the peace of the area. “This has become necessary as the situation has continued to threaten lives, property and peace in the area,” he said. Under the order, no movement is allowed in either community from 6 pm to 6 am daily. The statement also barred residents of both communities from entering or moving into the disputed areas “for any reason.” Security agencies were directed to enforce the curfew strictly. The government warned that violators would face the full weight of the law. “Defaulters will be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law,” the Commissioner said. The state government appealed to community leaders, youths and other stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign. It said it remained committed to ending the hostilities between the two communities. “This administration remains committed to restoring lasting peace between the two communities and appeals to leaders, youths and all stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign,” the statement said. Cobham added that the government would keep a close watch on developments in the area. “The government will continue to monitor the situation closely until normalcy returns in the area,” he said. item.title: Wolves 3-0 Derby County - fans' verdicts
item.description: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Tuesday's Championship match between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Derby County. Here are some of your comments: Wolves fans Alan: Our best team performance of the season. Yes, we still need to be more incisive with our finishing, but apart from a spirited opening 10 minutes by Derby we were never in trouble. Mane seems to have regained his confidence and for a small, young striker showed real strength in holding off a massive Derby defender to create the first goal. Armstrong was cool in taking his two goals and Tommy Doyle was superb in midfield. Andre, Krejci and Djiga were solid at the back and Trippier and Bueno were always dangerous on the wings. Fer Lopez is all energy despite having to cope with three of four defenders. Cesar's tactics are winning the fans over, what a change from the misery of last season. Peter: Despite the scoreline, poor finishing and decision-making in and around the box held Wolves back in a game they should have won 6-0. However, Cesar is forging a formidable team, arguably having at his disposal a squad with an outstanding depth of talented players who are technically the best in the Championship. Rob: Excellent all-round performance where the dominance translated into goals for once. The defensive midfield foundation of Andre and Doyle is a revelation and Mane had an excellent game. But we need to talk about Jordan James. He was instrumental in the last two goals by pulling the Derby midfield and defence all over the place. Our strongest team would include him starting somehow. Many have intimated Lopez is carrying an injury - if that is so, James could start in his stead whilst Peixoto works on a system that could include both of them as starters. Teams will then be pushed to keep both of them quiet and I believe there would be an even more sustainable uplift in performance. December's games will be a sterner test with better opposition but Wolves can be tougher and more ruthless on this evidence. [Cody Froggatt/Press Association] Derby fans Per: We are clearly not good enough for this league. Decent defending, but we kept losing the ball and hardly created any chances. We could have scored twice (Morris and Fuseini) in the opening minutes, but we didn't take our chances and in the end we were outplayed. Philip: Absolutely awful. Route one or misplaced passes trying to play out from the back. Completely lacking in confidence. I really am not sure if Eustace can dig us out of this rut. I'd like to hope he can but I'm really not sure. Dave: Heart and fight is missing in this team. Understand the issues the proposed takeover has caused and the injuries, but our goalkeeper, who's been injured himself, is our top player too often. Need to get stuck in and get their hands dirty.

item.title: Fairfield Union’s Andy Clark is the 2025 Eagle-Gazette Coach of the Year
item.description: LANCASTER — When this year’s group of Fairfield Union football seniors were in the seventh grade, they won one game, going 1-7. Fairfield Union coach Andy Clark refused to give up on them. He believed in them and raised their standard and refused to let them fall below it. The group steadily improved and they started winning, but this season was special. The Falcons showed a lot of perseverance, stuck together when things looked bleak, and came out on the side as champions. Clark helped lead Fairfield Union to its first Mid-State League-Buckeye Division championship in 20 years. Playing Hamilton Township in a must-win situation in Week 10 to gain a share of the league title, the Falcons were able to hold on for a 14-6 victory. Fairfield Union picked up its first-ever playoff win in 2025, qualified for the playoffs again this season and hosted a first-round game. The Falcons finished with a 6-1 league mark and went 8-3 overall. Because of his leadership, Clark is the 2026 Eagle-Gazette Football Coach of the Year. More: Fairfield Union clinches a share of the Mid-State League-Buckeye title He was thankful for the recognition but wanted to talk more about what the team accomplished and how their hard work enabled them to achieve what they did. “Football is the most team-oriented sport on planet Earth, so anytime individual awards are given out, it’s clearly a group effort,” Clark said. “You have to have players that have bought in. They set goals, and they worked to achieve those. For that to happen, a lot of good things had to be in place, and that’s what makes it the most rewarding.” What made it even more special for Clark was how far the team had come, especially the seniors. “It was a group that could have given up on themselves and each other, but they stuck together,” Clark said. “They continued to work hard, they pushed each other, and they have a tight bond. They shared in all that pain and disappointment when they were younger, and even early in their high school careers. They really worked their tails off and made improvements each year, and it led to this year. They were playing big games at the end of the season, and I don’t know without that tough beginning they would be where they are now. They dealt with a lot of adversity in their careers. It’s just a testament to them sticking together.” The fact that the Falcons were able to hang on and pull out such a huge victory over the Rangers in the last game of the regular season, with so much on the line, it all went back to Clark holding his team to a higher standard and the belief they could win big games. “They were so prepared for that game, and they were locked in,” Clark said. “It was just neat to see it all come together. I was happy for them to see how far they had come to get to that moment with so much on the line. It was so gratifying to see them celebrate after that game. It all went back to holding them to the standard that it takes to achieve the goals they wanted to achieve.

item.title: Lancaster’s Reynolds is 2026 Eagle-Gazette Defensive Player of the Year
item.description: LANCASTER — Lancaster senior linebacker Jackson Reynolds loves football. He is quiet by nature, but don’t let that fool you. When he steps between the lines, he becomes a wrecking machine, making tackles from sideline to sideline and punishing running backs and quarterbacks. At 6-foot-3, 210 pounds, Reynolds trained hard to get his body in the best shape it could be, and it paid off. He had a tremendous season and made his presence felt immediately by averaging double-digit tackles for the Golden Gales. Reynolds finished with a team-leading 113 total tackles, including 60 solos, 12 tackles for loss, a forced fumble, five pass breakups and a blocked kick. Thanks to his tremendous season, Reynolds was an obvious choice to be selected as the 2026 Eagle-Gazette Defensive Player of the Year. More: Lancaster’s Jackson Reynolds is the 2024 Eagle-Gazette Defensive Player of the Year “It means a lot to me, and I am very grateful,” Reynolds said of winning the award. “I know that I put in the work, and winning individual awards wasn't anything I was focused on. I was focused on helping my team win as many games as we could, but getting the award showed how much work I put in.” Reynolds, who also named the E-G Defensive Player of the Year as a sophomore, earned first team All-Central District honors and was first team All-Ohio Capital Conference-Buckeye Division, as well as being a team captain. “I was in the weight room every day trying to get stronger and faster, and ate the right way to gain weight,” Reynolds said. “I never really took any days off from lifting, and the days I took off, I was running and working on my speed trying to get faster and watching film to get smarter and trying to stop whoever we were playing.” Reynolds showed right away that he was different. In the season opener, he had 14 tackles against Hilliard Darby, followed that up with a season-high 18 tackles at Delaware Hayes and 13 tackles against Marysville to close out the nonconference three-game schedule with 45 tackles. He combined for 24 more tackles in the first two league games before suffering a knee injury in Week 6 against Pickerington Central. Even though he wasn't 100%, he continued to play and played at a high level. Reynolds, who has four college offers and is still being looked at by several big-time schools, showed a lot of mental fortitude throughout the season. “I learned a lot about myself, but mostly that I was mentally tough,” Reynolds said. “I became mentally tougher with everything that I had to go through. I had a great support system, and I give so much thanks to my family because they were there pushing me all the way and supporting me. With their support, it motivated me even more and made me work even harder.” Reynolds said he wouldn’t change a thing. item.title: Fairfield Union’s Clark is 2026 Eagle-Gazette Offensive Player of the Year
item.description: LANCASTER — Fairfield Union quarterback Dean Clark has that it factor. He is the type of player coaches love to coach. His teammates gravitate toward him and follow his lead. Clark was the clear-cut leader of the Falcons, and while he hasn’t always been the most vocal, he knew he had to be that guy to speak up and be that one player that each member of the team looked to, especially when things weren't going well. As it turned out, Clark is a natural leader and his confidence and belief fed into the whole team. A year after qualifying and winning their first-ever playoff game in school history, Clark and the Falcons had loftier goals this season. He helped lead Fairfield Union to a share of the Mid-State League-Buckeye Division championship, the school’s first league title in 20 years. Clark had an outstanding season as he led the Falcons to an 8-3 overall record. He accounted for 1,888 total yards and 21 touchdowns. He completed 79-of-128 passes for 1,337 yards and 15 touchdowns and rushed 114 times for 551 yards and six touchdowns. For his efforts, Clark was chosen as the 2026 Eagle-Gazette Offensive Player of the Year. More: Fairfield Union clinches a share of the Mid-State League-Buckeye title “It is a gratifying feeling,” Clark said of winning the player of the year award. “There are a lot of great players in the area, so receiving this recognition is special. It’s an individual award, but football is a team sport, and I had a lot of guys around me who helped, and I wouldn’t be receiving this if it weren’t for my teammates and coaches.” Clark also earned first-team All-MSL, was named the league’s Back of the Year and was first-team Southeast All-District. “I think having success last year showed what we could do and what we were capable of and that really pushed us in the offseason to set our goals high, as far a winning a league title and getting to the playoffs again,” Clark said. “For myself, I just really wanted to improve on being a leader, and being the quarterback, the guys are going to look to you when things aren’t going well. I wanted to speak up and take the reins, and I think I did a better job of that this year and was more vocal as a leader. “I wouldn’t say I am naturally a vocal leader. Before this year, I was quieter and a lead-by-example type of player, but not everyone responds to that. Some people need to be lifted, vocally, so I tried to improve on that. You have to step outside of your comfort zone, sometimes, and speak up. I did a better job of being more vocal, and guys responded to that.” Winning the league title wasn’t easy because the Falcons lost a midseason league game against Bloom-Carroll and were 1-1 in the MSL. Forced to win the rest of their league games, the Falcons rattled off five straight wins, including a must-win game in Week 10 against Hamilton Township. item.title: Alabama’s Nate Oats stays silent on LSU-SEC standoff, but rips ‘hypocritical’ coaches
item.description: David Leong-Imagn Images Alabama’s Nate Oats stays silent on LSU-SEC standoff, but rips ‘hypocritical’ coaches appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . People seldom feel sorry for Alabama, or any SEC school for that matter, but Crimson Tide basketball head coach Nate Oats is more convinced than ever that his program was wrongfully criticized for putting former G League player Charles Bediako on the roster last season. He takes serious issue with the villain narrative that swirled around Tuscaloosa, especially since eligibility controversy is quite commonplace now. Oats was already not in a great mood following his team’s 68-63 Players Era 16 loss versus Baylor, so what better way to blow off steam than by dwelling on the past and taking shots at his contemporaries . “A lot of those coaches wanted to speak on the Bediako thing, well, they’re doing the exact thing this year,” the two-time SEC champion said from Las Vegas, Nevada’s T-Mobile Arena, per BamaCentral’s Theodore Fernandez. “Yeah, it does bother me. They’re kind of hypocritical, to be honest with you.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Oats refrained from commenting on LSU, as the university faces possible expulsion from the SEC amid the league’s ongoing dispute with RJ Luis Jr. He had no problem snapping back against all the anti-Alabama rhetoric, however. The former SEC Coach of the Year believes he was unfairly condemned for taking advantage of the system, particularly because others are now following his lead. That being said, he may be forgetting just how unusual the Bediako situation was. The Canadian big man returned to Alabama last season after being out of college for almost three years. He played in the G League and therefore brought with him a competitive edge. Surprisingly, Charles Bediako did not make a huge impact in his second stint with the Tide. He averaged only 10.0 points and 4.6 rebounds across five games before being denied eligibility. It was hard to believe he made it that far. Despite a fairly blatant circumvention of collegiate athletic ethics, Alabama was not in danger of being ousted from the conference. LSU is not a victim, either, to be clear, but this notion that the Crimson Tide were mercilessly ripped apart ignores certain context. While Alabama basketball received significant backlash, it did not face severe consequences. Nate Oats is nevertheless annoyed and is taking the opportunity to speak his mind. Perhaps the Tide can unleash that frustration on the court, as they try to bounce back against Kansas State on Thanksgiving. item.title: 3 Reasons Mississippi State Could Cover Against Ole Miss in the Egg Bowl
item.description: Sep 26, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi State Bulldogs running back Fluff Bothwell (24) reacts after a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Egg Bowl always brings extra intensity, and this year’s rivalry matchup could be more competitive than the betting spread suggests. Ole Miss enters Friday’s showdown as a heavy favorite, with the Rebels favored by around 19 points. However, Mississippi State has a few reasons to believe it can keep the game closer than expected. The Bulldogs have struggled down the stretch, but rivalry games can be unpredictable. Here are three reasons Mississippi State could cover the spread against Ole Miss. 1. The Rivalry Factor Could Keep It Close There is always something different about the Egg Bowl. Records and rankings do not always matter when these two programs meet, and Mississippi State will have plenty of motivation to make life difficult for its biggest rival. Ole Miss is the better team on paper, but playing a rivalry game comes with added pressure. The Rebels will have to handle the atmosphere and expectations that come with being a heavy favorite. Mississippi State does not necessarily need to win this game to make it successful. If the Bulldogs can keep the score within reach, force a few mistakes and make Ole Miss work for every possession, they have a chance to cover a spread approaching three touchdowns. 2. Ole Miss Has Defensive Weaknesses Mississippi State Can Attack One area that could give Mississippi State an opportunity is the Ole Miss defense. The Rebels have struggled at times against opposing offenses, particularly when teams are able to sustain drives and take advantage of defensive mistakes. Mississippi State has an opportunity to attack through the air and make Ole Miss defend multiple situations. The Bulldogs have shown some ability to find success on passing downs, which could become important if they are forced into obvious throwing situations. Quarterback Parker Puckett will need to make smart decisions and avoid turnovers. Mississippi State cannot afford to give Ole Miss extra possessions, especially against an offense capable of putting points on the board quickly. If the Bulldogs can put together a few long scoring drives, they could make this matchup much more interesting. 3. A Big Spread Gives Mississippi State Some Room The biggest reason to consider Mississippi State against the spread is simply the size of the number. Ole Miss is favored by approximately 19 points, meaning the Rebels must win comfortably for bettors backing them to cash. Ole Miss has the offensive talent to create separation, but covering a spread that large requires consistency for four quarters. item.title: CAF releases finalists for 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award (Full list)
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has released the five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi, Senegal’s Sadio Mané and three other players making the shortlist. The final nominees were selected from an initial list of 10 players based on their performances for club and country during the period under consideration. Morocco has three representatives on the list, while Senegal has two, reflecting the countries’ strong performances in the period. Hakimi, who plays for French champions Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the award after helping the club win the UEFA Champions League and French Ligue 1 title. The Moroccan defender also captained his national team during its campaigns at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is also in contention for a third title after helping Senegal win the 2025 AFCON. The Al-Nassr forward was named the tournament’s Best Player in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Senegal’s triumph. Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz earned a place on the shortlist following his performances for Morocco, particularly at the 2025 AFCON, where he won the Golden Boot with five goals. Villarreal midfielder Pape Gueye also made the list after scoring the winning goal in extra time as Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the AFCON final in Rabat. His performances at the tournament also earned him a place in the Best XI. Completing the shortlist is Morocco’s Ismael Saibari, who played an important role in his country’s run to the AFCON final, including scoring against Cameroon in the quarter-finals. The winner will be announced at the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos. The ceremony is expected to begin at 7pm Nigerian time. The CAF Awards will return to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition. item.title: Meta unveils $700,000 AI grant for Nigerian startups
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Meta has announced a $700,000 artificial intelligence (AI) grant programme for startups and developers in Nigeria and six other countries, as part of efforts to accelerate AI innovation and expand access to emerging technologies. The programme, scheduled to commence in 2027, will cover Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), according to a statement issued by the company on Tuesday. Meta said the grant would support startups and developers building solutions using its AI tools and wearable technologies. The company also announced the launch of a new hub designed to provide educational resources and information on its AI developments, partnerships and innovation initiatives across Africa, the Middle East and Turkey. The hub will operate through three learning programmes: AI Academy, AI Literacy and AI for Small and Medium-sized Businesses. The programmes are designed for students, developers, entrepreneurs and business professionals, with Meta targeting more than five million beneficiaries across the three regions over the next three years. Meta’s Vice-President of Public Policy for Africa, the Middle East and Turkey, Kojo Boakye, said the initiatives were designed to equip developers and entrepreneurs with the skills, resources and support needed to build AI solutions that address challenges in their communities. “AI’s value will be judged by the real impact it has on people’s lives,” Boakye said. “Across our region, people are building solutions around the languages they speak, the businesses they run and the challenges their communities face. “The Impact Grant and Hub are about giving more builders the support, skills and resources to turn those ideas into useful products and services. We want people here to help shape AI’s future, not simply use what others have built.” In another initiative, Meta announced the AMET AI Awards 2026, with more than $100,000 in prizes across seven categories to recognise outstanding AI innovations. The company said the awards would recognise finalists from its AI Academy and Wearables Studio programmes, including students, developers and startups. The award categories include Wearables Innovation of the Year, AI Builder of the Year, Emerging Innovator of the Year and Startup of the Year. Others are AI for Accessibility and Inclusion, AI for Social and Economic Impact, and People’s Choice, which will be decided through a live vote by attendees at the summit. Meta said the awards would recognise projects leveraging AI-powered technologies to address everyday needs, improve access to opportunities and services, and promote social and economic development. item.title: Opel and Citroen exit is not a betrayal of Formula E, but a major blow at the worst possible time
item.description: Motorsport photo What many had feared has unfortunately come to pass. In light of the substantial financial hole that emerged at the end of 2025 and the losses recorded in the third quarter of this year, Stellantis has decided to close almost all of its programmes, including those in Formula E, which at the end of 2027 will lose Citroen and Opel. However, it is important to understand that this decision goes beyond a single category and is not a barometer of the championship's health. This is not a betrayal of Formula E, of what it represents or its value, as the simultaneous departure from the WEC with Peugeot shows. Rather, it is a reflection of the very complex moment the entire European automotive sector is going through. Read Also: Peugeot quits WEC, Citroen and Opel to wind down Formula E programmes Stellantis has not yet reported its full financial results for 2026, with the latest statement currently stopping at the third-quarter losses, but the company's senior management has repeatedly said that in 2027 the rising price of raw materials could cost not millions, but billions. The exit from racing programmes starts here: the problem is not motorsport, but what lies upstream. On the contrary, Formula E was conceived as a financially sustainable category, precisely to attract the major manufacturers. It is a model that worked for years, to the point that today there is no shortage of leading brands. However, for a series whose main strength is in manufacturers' commitment, losing two brands in one go is the equivalent of a well-placed right hook. It is easy to understand why sporting projects are the first to be cut in difficult times, but both Opel and Citroen have already invested a significant part of the budget allocated to the 2027 season, so much so that they will contest the season. The economic effects of this decision, therefore, will not be immediate, not to mention the penalties that will have to be paid to Formula E linked to the early exit from the championship. “Formula E will work closely with Stellantis to manage an orderly transition, also addressing the contractual obligations and financial aspects linked to the early exit, while it will continue to assess the strong interest shown by new manufacturers and teams intending to join the grid in the coming seasons,” read a statement released by the electric series. Citroen Racing Citroen e-CX Citroen Racing Citroen e-CX Indeed, and this is where the real paradox of the matter emerges. For Gen4, Stellantis had chosen to increase investment with the aim of returning to the top, considering its importance to its motorsport programme and also it being the one closest in terms of benefits for its production products. This is also shown by the decision to endorse Opel's entry only a few months ago with its own licence, made possible through an investment of millions of euros. item.title: Como join the Serie A sides eyeing January move for Joshua Zirkzee
item.description: Como join the Serie A sides eyeing January move for Joshua Zirkzee Como have joined the growing list of Serie A sides interested in signing Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee during the January transfer window. Zirkzee is a transfer target for a number of Italian clubs after struggling for favour at Old Trafford. The Dutchman has not started a Premier League game this season and has failed to earn a regular role under multiple managers, with Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick all unconvinced. He has continued to be overlooked this season, despite Benjamin Sesko’s absence through injury. The Slovenian striker has been ruled out until January, but that has not aided Zirkzee’s quest for minutes. Zirkzee is expected to hold talks with Mauricio Pochettino about his status in the new manager’s plans, though there’s an expectation that he will be allowed to leave. According to Sky Sports , Como have joined Napoli in leading the chase for the 25-year-old. Zirkzee had an impressive Serie A spell prior to moving to the Premier League and was named the division’s Young Player of the Season after scoring 11 league goals for Bologna in 2023/24. Roma and Juventus have also tracked Zirkzee, who was a target for Everton on summer Deadline Day, but United rejected the loan offer late in the window. item.title: A tale of two halves for Blades - fans' verdicts
item.description: [BBC] [Press Association] We asked for your thoughts after Sheffield United scored a 90th-minute equaliser to draw 1-1 with Southampton in the Championship on Tuesday. Here are some of your comments: United fans Julian: Great second-half performance where we were totally dominant. Why oh why did we not turn up in the first half? Jordan Ayew my MOM. What an assist plus lots of other creative bits of play. We outplayed Southampton in the second half and continuously put them on the back foot. If we can do that for 90+ minutes we should get that play-off place going forward. Matt: A really bizarre game of football, truly two completely different halves of football. Southampton strolled through the first half without breaking a sweat, but also not creating much more than the goal. Then Sheff U just blew Southampton away in the second half, with Ayew and Burrows being clear stand-outs. Could have been 0-3, 3-1, 3-3... but will gladly take the point in the end. Jason: One of the worst performances of the season in the first half, one of the best performances second half. Came away from a draw tonight happier than I did from a win on Saturday. Captain Blade: Deserved point, thankfully they went defensive second half.

item.title: Taylor Lewan thinks Caleb Williams could do what no NFL player has ever done before
item.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images Caleb Williams is only in the midst of his third season in the NFL but he is already being touted to achieve big things. The young quarterback suffered a hamstring strain back in September but has since shone upon his return to help the Chicago Bears go 8-2. Amid his impressive form, Taylor Lewan has now floated the idea that Williams could be named the NFL MVP and win the Comeback Player of the Year award in 2026. Speaking via a podcast this week, he said: “Caleb Williams, though. Tell you what, stud. MVP-calibre guy. Comeback Player of the Year in the same year.” One of his fellow hosts then pointed out: “Yep. That would be the first time ever,” to which Lewan responded: “That would be unbelievable. He’s a phenomenal quarterback and talent.” How Caleb Williams compares to other MVP candidates Because of his injury, Williams has only played seven games so far this season. So, it is hard to judge him on overall stats like passing yards, which he ranks 25th in the league for with 1,727, and passing touchdowns, which he ranks 19th for (10) When it comes to per game stats, the Bears ace has a 68.3% completion rate, which is the eighth-highest in the NFL and below several MVP candidates like Joe Burrow (74.2%) and Brock Purdy (71.0%). Elsewhere, he is throwing for 246.7 yards per game. That is the 11th-highest total in the league but again, still off the pace of big names like Purdy (262.4), Burrow (309.5), Patrick Mahomes (270.9) and Jordan Love (283.8). Williams’ average yards per pass attempt isn’t that amazing either. His 7.9 average (10th overall) puts him below Lamar Jackson (10.0), Purdy (9.0), Trevor Lawrence (8.4), Josh Allen (8.4), Burrow (8.1) and more. So, while he is having a good season and should have plenty of years ahead of him in the NFL to keep getting better, he doesn’t really look to be on the same level as other top quarterbacks just yet. item.title: Arsenal told to pay £100m to sign rival’s attacker
item.description: Arsenal told to pay £100m to sign rival’s attacker Bournemouth Stand Firm on Eli Junior Kroupi as Manchester United Weigh Nathan Collins Move Manchester United’s search for experience and leadership in defence is gathering pace ahead of January, with TALKSPORT reporting that Brentford captain Nathan Collins is prominent on the club’s shortlist. The 25-year-old has emerged as a leading domestic option as Mauricio Pochettino looks to address a damaging start to the season and a back line that has become a major concern inside Old Trafford. United’s recruitment team are understood to be exploring the home market for players who can arrive with minimal adaptation time. Collins appeals on that front, both for his Premier League experience and his standing at Brentford. Fulham’s Calvin Bassey has also been considered, although expectations are that he will commit to a new contract, while Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite remains admired but is viewed as a difficult deal to execute in the middle of the campaign, largely because of cost. Photo IMAGO Manchester United Defensive Overhaul Moves Forward The urgency around United’s plans appears to have accelerated. What had been shaping up as a summer rebuild in defence now looks increasingly likely to be brought forward. With Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martinez all due to be out of contract next summer, there had already been a strategic review of the department. However, the scale of the team’s defensive issues has forced a rethink. Conceding 34 goals already, a total described as the worst across Europe’s top five leagues, has sharpened minds at board level. That context explains why Collins is being discussed so seriously, even if Brentford are highly likely to insist on a substantial fee. His contract runs until 2029, which leaves the west London club in a strong negotiating position and means United would probably need to pay well above market comfort to make progress in January. Eli Junior Kroupi Price Tag Sends Bournemouth Message Elsewhere, Bournemouth have made their position emphatically clear on Eli Junior Kroupi. The club have no intention of sanctioning a January sale and have placed a £100 million valuation on the 20-year-old. That number feels designed as much to deter interest as to establish any immediate negotiating framework, particularly given the calibre of clubs monitoring him. Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are all credited with serious interest in the winger, whose development has continued at speed. Bournemouth’s internal stance is that he will stay at least until the summer, a decision that reflects both his importance to the squad and the growing sense that his value could rise further. Kroupi has scored 13 goals in 37 Premier League appearances, strong output for a young attacker still building his top-flight career. There is also an expectation that, if he does leave the south coast in future, PSG may hold a significant advantage. The suggestion is that the pla

item.title: Refereeing chief defends red card decision in Liverpool win
item.description: Refereeing chief defends red card decision in Liverpool win Leny Yoro Red Card Overturned After Liverpool Defeat as Howard Webb Stands by Anfield Decision Manchester United have won their appeal against Leny Yoro’s early dismissal at Anfield, meaning the defender is now free to play against Brentford. The decision removes the immediate sporting consequence for Mauricio Pochettino’s side, but it has not brought full agreement on the incident itself. Yoro was sent off inside the opening eight minutes of United’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool after colliding with Alexander Isak as the forward broke through on goal. The dismissal proved a major turning point in a one-sided contest, with Liverpool taking full control and United unable to recover after going down to 10 men. While the Football Association has now rescinded the red card, Howard Webb has made clear that the original on-field decision remains defensible in his view. That leaves an unusual split, with the suspension lifted but the refereeing chief still publicly backing the judgment made during the game. Appeal Success Offers United a Boost United’s appeal has at least ensured Yoro avoids a ban at a time when availability matters. Pochettino had reacted angrily in the aftermath of the match, arguing the challenge did not warrant a dismissal and pointing to perceived inconsistency in similar situations elsewhere. For United, that appeal outcome is important ahead of a demanding run of fixtures, starting with Brentford in the league and followed by a Champions League meeting with Sporting CP. It also spares Yoro, one of the club’s key young defenders, from further disruption after a difficult afternoon at Anfield. The broader debate, however, has centred on whether the challenge denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity. That is where Webb’s explanation becomes significant, because he believes the referee had sufficient grounds to reach for a red card even if others interpreted the sequence differently. Howard Webb Explains Why Decision Stood Speaking publicly about the moment, Webb said, “Firstly, I want to say, I think this is a really decisive decision by the referee, Sam Barrott. We know it’s clearly a foul. I don’t think there’s any dispute about that.” He then set out the framework officials use in such cases, adding, “And we also know that it’s outside the penalty area. we’re thinking about the sanction, aren’t we, that’s why we’re talking about this.” Webb’s breakdown focused on the standard criteria for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity, including direction of play, distance from goal, covering defenders and whether the attacker would likely retain control of the ball. On those points, he said, “Is it a denial of an obvious goal scoring opportunity? Four considerations officials have to think about. direction of play, it’s definitely going towards the goal. It’s not going out wide. Proximity from goal, well, it’s just outside the penalty area. the location of other defenders. Well

item.title: After further review, Kent State football win turns into a loss
item.description: YPSILANTI, MICH. — Upon further review, Kent State's 2026 college football season ended in the most brutal way possible. Ethan Thanthanavong's winning 14-yard touchdown pass to Wayne Harris on fourth down with one second left was overturned, and the Golden Flashes left Rynearson Stadium with a 17-12 loss to Eastern Michigan on Nov. 24. A television replay showed Harris getting one foot inbounds as he caught the ball in the back of the end zone. He appeared to have possession as he landed. After a replay review, the officials determined that Harris did not have possession. The Flashes finished the season at 3-9 overall and 2-6 in the Mid-American Conference. The overturned call cost Harris an opportunity to become only the fourth 1,000-yard receiver in program history. He caught five passes for 125 yards and finished the season with 60 catches for 988 yards. Brendyn Smith scored Kent State's two touchdowns. He caught a 17-yard touchdown pass from Thanthanavong and returned a kickoff 100 yards for a TD. This article originally appeared on Akron Beacon Journal: After further review, Kent State football win turns into a loss

item.title: Musiala first examined due to absence-like symptoms after new contract
item.description: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala sits on the bench prior to the start of the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and 1. FC Cologne at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Musiala first examined due to absence-like symptoms after new contract») Tom Weller/dpa Bayern Munich clarified that Jamal Musiala was first examined due to absence-like symptoms in April 2025, and therefore after he signed a new contract with the club. "As there have been many rumours in recent days, FC Bayern and 11WINS, the agency representing Jamal, wish to clarify: Jamal Musiala was first examined on 22 April 2025 due to absence-like symptoms," the club said in a statement on Wednesday. "This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared." Musiala signed a contract extension until June 2030 in February 2025. The player's health condition and contract situation have been under the spotlight in recent weeks after public remarks from club officials. After collapsing twice during pre-season, Musiala said he has been affected by absence seizures, a form of epilepsy, and has missed some of the campaign because of it. He has struggled for his best form when he has played. Honorary president Uli Hoeness spoke of a dilemma for the club, while chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen raised the prospect of talks with Musiala's management and family. Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge also questioned the 23-year-old's lucrative contract signed just last year if he does not hit the same heights as earlier in his career. Doctors have said there is no reason his form should suffer. Bayern had a meeting with Musiala's management on Tuesday and the club spoke of constructive talks. "A constructive meeting took place between FC Bayern Munich and the management of Jamal Musiala yesterday (Tuesday). For both sides, the player's health comes above everything else. Musiala is being given full support on his road back," Bayern said. The club added that talks with Musiala's management will continue "in partnership and in confidence."

item.title: Zamfara: Bandits kill two headmasters, 13 others, abduct residents
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Armed bandits have killed 15 people, including two primary school headmasters and an 11-month-old baby, in separate attacks on communities in Zamfara State. The attacks, which occurred in Tungan Janbuzu and Madanbaji communities, also left several residents abducted, according to a report by the BBC Hausa Service. The two headmasters, identified as Kabiru Salisu and Shehu Umar, both aged 35, were reportedly killed in an ambush at Janbuzu. A resident of the community, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 4pm, following the escape of some kidnapped residents from their captors. He explained that the bandits had earlier abducted some locals from Janbuzu and kept them in captivity, forcing them to work for their captors. According to him, the kidnappers had demanded a ransom of N300,000, which was subsequently delivered to them at a location near Kiawa. He said the bandits collected the money but later drove the person who delivered it away, claiming that the payment was meant for recharge cards and fuel. The resident further narrated that the bandits had taken six captives into the bush, tied them up and left them under the supervision of a young boy while they went to Aboro to purchase drugs and other supplies. However, the captives reportedly managed to untie themselves, overpower their guard, seize his gun and escape after beating him. The resident said the escape angered other members of the gang, who were reportedly hiding on a nearby farm. He said the armed men subsequently ambushed the two headmasters near a location known as Gora, seized their mobile phones and shot them dead. The resident, however, said kidnapping incidents had reduced considerably in the area, except in communities located close to the forests and bushes where the bandits operate. He expressed concern over the continued vulnerability of residents in remote settlements, despite the reported reduction in kidnapping incidents. item.title: Marshall Faulk shared his Parkinson's diagnosis for one selfless reason | Opinion
item.description: BATON ROUGE, La. – Eric Dickerson warned him. After Marshall Faulk hung up his spikes following an amazing 12-year career as one of the greatest running backs in NFL history, Dickerson told him what to expect as a former football player in retirement. Those old football injuries, Dickerson cautioned, never really go away. “Eric warned me,” Faulk, 53, told USA TODAY Sports during a wide-ranging interview in his office at Southern University , where he is winding down his first season as a rookie head coach. "Like when I retired, I think I was 33, he said, 'When you get to be 43 or 48, check back with me then.'" It brought back the memory of a conversation I had a few years ago with Dickerson, himself one of the greatest running backs ever, when he mentioned how difficult it was for him to get a good night’s sleep. He told me about nagging aches from various injuries – including from a shot he took in the chest from a late hit after scoring a touchdown decades ago – that sometimes popped up from nowhere. When I told Faulk about my chat with his fellow Hall of Famer, he grinned and nodded. “That is so true,” Faulk said. “I think at 48, I tore my Achilles. I was like, ‘Damn!’ ” What were you doing? “Nothing, man, nothing. Seriously.” You weren’t on the golf course? “Nothing. Literally, I took a step down. Pop. Nothing,” Faulk described. MORE JARRETT BELL: Forget Parkinson's. Marshall Faulk is building a football power at Southern | Exclusive Why Marshall Faulk revealed Parkinson's diagnosis The foot has long been fully healed, yet Faulk has gone public with his current health challenge. He recently revealed that he was diagnosed about a year-and-half ago with the early stages of Parkinson’s disease. He’s so upbeat about his prospects for managing this – which includes medication – and that he has had no progressive symptoms. According to experts, Parkinson’s is considered a risk factor, but not a direct cause, for neurological decline. Still, it may be natural to wonder – on the heels of former All-Pro running back Chris Johnson’s disclosure in July that he is battling ALS , which has robbed him of his ability to speak and left him bound to a wheelchair; and with former running back Roger Craig using his Hall of Fame induction speech in August to announce that he has been dealing with vascular dementia – whether Faulk’s Parkinson’s diagnosis is linked to football. The same shocks to the body absorbed in football that can blow out knees and dislocate ankles, for example, can also rattle brains. Faulk’s discovery began on the golf course, when stiffness in joints prompted him to seek evaluation. “You know, I have some stiffness in my wrist, my hand, my elbow,” he said. “At times, it would just freeze up. I thought, ‘Hey, that’s par for the course. I played professional football.’ And then to find out it’s something else, it’s like, ‘OK, yeah.’ ” Marshall Faulk NFL career stats Faulk was 33 when he played his final season with the St. Louis Rams in 2005

item.title: ‘Let them learn’ – Why Peyton Manning is desperate for young QBs to break his rookie record
item.description: Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images Peyton Manning had a historic rookie year filled with record-setting numbers, but the Broncos and Colts legend is ready to pass the mantle on to a new young quarterback. Manning’s 1998 rookie season was phenomenal, as he set five new records as a rookie quarterback in what many consider the most dominant debut season in NFL history. However, of those five records, only one stands to this day, and Manning is just waiting for the day a young quarterback snatches that record from him. Peyton Manning once revealed the real reason he wants his NFL rookie record broken During an appearance on the Kittle Things podcast a few months ago, Peyton Manning jokingly explained to George Kittle why he is ready for his last remaining record from his rookie year – the record for most interceptions thrown by a rookie – to be broken. He noted that coaches don’t allow their rookie quarterbacks to make mistakes and stay in the game, and that is standing in the way of his record possibly being broken. “Am I proud to hold the NFL interception rookie record? No,” Manning said on Kittle’s podcast earlier this year. “Would I like to get it broken? Yes. Do I think it should be with 17 games now? Yes. Do the coaches take the rookies that are struggling out too early? 100%. “Leave them in there. Let them learn. I’m over it, as you can tell. But that would be my rookie mistake. Respect it, but don’t over-respect it where you kind of get yourself out of whack.” For those unaware, Manning currently holds the record for the most interceptions thrown by a rookie quarterback in a single season with 28. In fact, Manning set five records in his rookie year – most interceptions thrown, most attempts, most completed passes, most passing yards, and most passing touchdowns. Out of these records, all except his interceptions record have been broken, with his completed passes and passing touchdowns thrown records being the last to stand till Justin Herbert broke both of them in the 2020 season. item.title: Newcastle under ‘no pressure’ to sell Lewis Hall and rule out January deal
item.description: Newcastle under ‘no pressure’ to sell Lewis Hall and rule out January deal Newcastle United are under no pressure to sell key players in the January transfer window, amid interest from Manchester United in Lewis Hall. Manchester United have been linked with a move to sign Hall in the upcoming transfer window, as Mauricio Pochettino looks to sign a new left-back. United enquired about the England international in the summer, but were told the 22-year-old was not for sale. Newcastle are set to communicate a similar message in January, with their position strengthened by summer business, and Hall’s recently-signed new contract. Newcastle sold Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Sando Tonali for upwards of £235m combined in the summer and have no financial pressure to make further sales. According to the iPaper, Newcastle have room to invest without the need to sell key figures. Chief financial officer Simon Capper confirmed the club can continue investing after summer sales strengthened their finances. He said the summer sales were designed to fall in line with UEFA’s regulations as the Magpies look to become a consistent European presence. “It’s a really good place to be in, and allows the club freedom to go again when we want to,” he said. “It’s a matter of: if you want to be in Europe, you’ve got to play their (UEFA’s) game. The club had maxed out its credit card (before that). Capper added that there is “no imperative to sell somebody in January, and we don’t have to do anything we don’t want to do. It gives us the ability to invest again at a proportionate level, depending on what European competition you qualify for.” Read More – Man Utd target Bassey in talks over new Fulham deal See Also – Five of the best Premier League away kits in 2026/27 Follow The Football Faithful on Social Media: Facebook | Instagram | Twitter | YouTube | TikTok

item.title: Michael Redd gives ‘monster’ Karl-Anthony Towns his flowers for powerful start
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images The New York Knicks haven’t had the perfect start to the 2026-27 NBA season, but one ex-NBA All-Star has highlighted how good Karl-Anthony Towns has been. The New York Knicks had a bit of championship hangover to start the 2026-27 NBA season. The reigning champs won six and lost six of their first 12 games, but have since won five straight. While stars on the team like Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby have struggled, one player is on fire. Karl-Anthony Towns was instrumental in helping the Knicks win it all last season. And despite the struggles of his teammates, he is performing at an elite level. Towns is leading the entire league in rebounding, and has notched double-doubles in every single one of the 16 games he has played. And finally, someone is ready to show him some love. Michael Redd says Karl-Anthony Towns should be praised for the ‘player he is’ after excellent start Towns is averaging 21.8 points, 13.9 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 16 appearances for the Knicks, shooting 54.3 percent from the field and 41.5 percent from three-point range. He has been effective on both ends of the floor, and has been performing consistently well. Former Milwaukee Bucks star Michael Redd has now highlighted KAT’s start to the season, showering him with some well-deserved praise. “Easy to call KAT’s season a championship high,” Redd wrote in an X post. “We’ve seen that movie before. A guy has a monster June, gets marketed all summer, then the season tips and he crashes right back to earth. Happens every year. Look around his own locker room, a couple faces of that title run came out ice cold, one even got benched. “Not KAT. Dude never dipped. Leading the whole NBA in rebounds, career-long double-double streak, scoring as efficient as he’s ever been. Are we actually watching his (really high) ceiling right now? Because if this is it, wow. The man has gotten so, so good. “We spend so much time talking about what he isn’t that we forget to give him flowers for the incredible player and man that he is. KAT’s having a monster year, in the middle of a heck of a career, and we get to watch it happen. Appreciate it while it’s here. Because it’s powerful!” This is a fantastic sentiment from Redd, and one that is sure to resonate with Knicks fans. Towns is also performing in a way that will make it difficult for New York to not pay him soon. He could be a free agent at the end of this season, and his greatness to start the year might just see him get paid. item.title: Wales and West Ham's Morgan suffers serious injury
item.description: Ffion Morgan joined West Ham from Bristol City in 2025 [FAW] Wales and West Ham winger Ffion Morgan is facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury. Morgan has undergone surgery having been helped off during West Ham's Women's Super League win over Charlton earlier this month. The 26-year-old is now likely to miss the rest of the season. "Ffion will now begin her rehabilitation programme under the supervision of the club's medical team," a West Ham statement said. The injury also makes Morgan a major doubt for next summer's Women's World Cup, should Wales qualify. Rhian Wilkinson's side take on Norway in a two-legged play-off final next week as they bid to reach the tournament for the first time in the nation's history. Morgan, who has 56 caps, is an international regular and would be a shoo-in for the Wales squad if fit. Five return for Wales' World Cup play-off final Home World Cup can inspire Wales' future stars She joined West Ham on a two-year deal in 2025 after her contract at Bristol City expired. Morgan has also played for Cardiff City, Coventry United and Crystal Palace. She suffered an ACL injury while playing for Wales Under-19s as a teenager, while she had only recently returned to action for West Ham after another lengthy fitness lay-off. Wales face Norway at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later. Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway may not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer. The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway.

item.title: Massimiliano Allegri backs 'extraordinary' Kevin De Bruyne to stay at Napoli after emotional Man City return
item.description: SSC Napoli v Torino FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Kevin De Bruyne received a hero's welcome on his emotional return to the Etihad Stadium as Napoli held Manchester City to a 2-2 Champions League draw. Following the match, Napoli boss Massimiliano Allegri praised the midfielder as "extraordinary" and addressed mounting speculation linking him with a January move to PSV Eindhoven. Emotional Etihad return ends in entertaining draw De Bruyne made an emotional return to the Etihad Stadium as Napoli earned a 2-2 draw against City in the Champions League league phase. The home supporters greeted their former talisman with a hero's welcome before applauding him off the pitch in the second half. De Bruyne departed City in the summer of 2025 to join Napoli on a free transfer. Facing his old club, the 35-year-old played 75 minutes before Allegri replaced him with Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa. As De Bruyne walked to the touchline, the City crowd rose to give him a warm standing ovation. Allegri hails extraordinary De Bruyne after ovation Speaking to Sky Sport Italia after the full-time whistle, Allegri admitted he felt a pang of sadness when deciding to withdraw the veteran midfielder. Despite his advancing years, the Belgian's technical composure clearly left a lasting impression on his manager. "Unfortunately, age waits for no man, but he is an extraordinary player," Allegri said. "It made me sad to take him off today, as he rarely makes a mistake with the ball at his feet. Players like De Bruyne and Luka Modric, for those who love football and admire the sport, they represent something special." Transfer rumours swirl around veteran Belgian playmaker De Bruyne's sentimental night in England arrived amid mounting speculation over his next career move. Although the Belgium international remains under contract with Napoli until June 2027, multiple reports suggest he could depart Italy when the January transfer window opens. PSV have reportedly opened high-level talks to bring the playmaker to the Netherlands six months before his deal expires. Everton have also been linked with a surprise winter approach for the midfielder. De Bruyne has remained a regular starter for Napoli in Serie A this season, contributing four goals and one assist, yet his contract situation has made him an attractive mid-season target. Napoli boss expects De Bruyne to stay Despite the growing noise surrounding PSV's pursuit, Allegri expressed confidence that De Bruyne will not walk away from Naples mid-season. The Italian tactician stressed that talks will take place internally while praising the midfielder's attitude. "We'll discuss it with the club, but he is a very professional lad, and I think he will remain until June," Allegri assured. With active negotiations reportedly continuing ahead of the winter market, the coming weeks will decide whether PSV can tempt De Bruyne away early or if Allegri gets his wish to keep the playmaker until the end of the campaign.

item.title: Injuries at QB give Michigan State freshman Kayd Coffman shot to learn
item.description: EAST LANSING – The moment Kayd Coffman and every college football player dreams of arrived sooner than expected, with the picturesque San Gabriel Mountains as the backdrop. Rose Bowl Stadium in Pasadena, California provided an iconic setting for the Michigan State football freshman quarterback’s starting debut, even though it wasn’t the iconic New Year’s Day game. Still, it was a long way from the fields in West Michigan that Coffman called home not even 10 months earlier. RELATED: Couch: 5 quick takes on MSU football's finale, the Big Ten's plight and College Football Playoff “That was definitely a sweet moment, something to remember,” Coffman said Tuesday, Nov. 24. “It was fun throughout that week, just being able to play at such a historic spot.” With injuries to starter Alessio Milivojevic and backup Cam Fancher , the Kentwood native showed signs of his developing talents with the expected mistakes of youth and inexperience in the Spartans’ 28-10 loss to No. 10 UCLA on Oct. 24 . Less than a month later, Milivojevic's and Fancher's injuries again gave Coffman a start in Friday’s 45-7 loss to No. 14 Oregon , his first at home for the school he never wavered from playing for, even with a coaching change last year before he signed. Coach Pat Fitzgerald did not reveal Monday, Nov. 23, what might happen at quarterback when MSU (3-8, 1-7 Big Ten) travels to Rutgers (3-8, 2-6) for the finale of his and Coffman’s debut seasons in green and white on Saturday (4:15 p.m., Big Ten Network). The first-year coach, however, didn't hide his praise for what he has seen in his young QB thrust into duty early in his career. “Kayd’s growth from UCLA week to last week: much more comfortable, a lot more confident,” Fitzgerald said. “I thought in his prep – not that he did a bad job at UCLA – but you could just tell that he had done it and was prepared to be the starter. It wasn’t his first time, so that was great to see. I thought he settled in pretty well.” Against the Bruins , Coffman became just the third true freshman to start at quarterback in MSU history, completing his first four passes for 42 yards, including a 14-yard screen pass touchdown to running back Kenneth Williams. But he misfired on his final six throws, including a misread for an interception, and was replaced by redshirt freshman Leo Hannan late in the third quarter. Milivojevic, who had started 11 straight games before missing the UCLA game with a right thumb injury, returned after a bye week to start the Spartans ’ 15-6 win at Michigan on Nov. 7. However, the third-year sophomore suffered a left arm injury against Washington a week later and missed the rest of that game. Fancher, a sixth-year senior transfer, had returned from a four-game absence and took over, but he aggravated his right knee injury late in the third quarter. item.title: A point at home enough to save Skubala?
item.description: [BBC] [David Davies/Press Association] We asked for your thoughts after Bristol City ended their winless run at home with a 1-1 draw against Wrexham. Here are some of your comments: Roger: Much better second half. Ballard and Tolaj should start every time. Clear foul on Twine when he was through. Red card and penalty. Should be enough to save Skubala for a few weeks if this keeps up. West Brom away next. Difficult match. Paul: A point at home against a relatively poor Wrexham side not good enough. Skubala has to go. Jo: I think the first half was very uncomfortable to watch, both defending and then when in possession. Everything looked so sloppy. Second half could only be, and was, better. They were unlucky a few times hitting the post. And most probably feel hard done by with a draw. Although from my position in the stands it looked a blatant push in the back [on Twine], and should have been a penalty. Tim: The players probably did just enough to keep Skubala in his job until the weekend. City started really poorly and again sat off the opposition and let them dictate play, but at least we began to move the ball more quickly as the game went on. We didn't create many clear chances and still aren't playing to Tolaj's strengths but at least we played a front two at home. Very frustrating watching him and Ballard making run after run in behind and no one attempting to hit them with early balls.

item.title: When did Nigerian law prescribe death for election rigging? — APC’s Morka asks Obi, NDC
item.description: By Bayo Wahab The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Felix Morka, has questioned the legal basis for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC)’s “rig and die” slogan, asking when Nigerian law prescribed the death penalty for electoral offences. Morka said anyone accused of rigging an election should be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law, rather than subjected to punishment determined by political parties or their supporters. The APC spokesman spoke on News Central on Wednesday while reacting to allegations of violence by NDC supporters against members of the ruling party. His comments followed remarks by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, who had defended the slogan during an interview with Channels Television after the party’s town hall meeting in Taraba State on Tuesday. Obi had dismissed concerns over the message, insisting that the supporters were opposed to election rigging, not political campaigns. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” Obi said. However, reacting to the explanation, Morka said the slogan was inflammatory and questioned the implication of allowing individuals to determine who had rigged an election and should therefore die. “Now, what does that mean? What message are you sending when you appoint yourself as custodians of elections, and therefore anyone you consider to have rigged an election — because that’s a subjective standard — should die,” he said. Morka said he had watched a video in which Obi defended the statement, adding that the NDC candidate had acknowledged that the message was “rig and die” rather than “campaign and die”. The APC spokesman then challenged Obi and the NDC to explain the legal justification for such a position. “So, if somebody rigs an election, since when did Nigerian law prescribe the death penalty for rigging an election?” he asked. Morka maintained that anyone suspected of electoral malpractice should be apprehended and made to face the consequences provided by law. “I think as a lawyer and as a citizen, that anyone who rigs an election should be apprehended and be made to face the law as provided by the law, not as provided by Peter Obi or the NDC stalwarts who make this very incendiary comment,” he said. Beyond the slogan, Morka also accused the NDC of making unsubstantiated allegations of violence against the APC without formally reporting the incidents to the police or seeking investigations by independent authorities. “So when the NDC comes out and they make allegations, if you look at all the allegations they make, there’s not one that they have managed or even attempted to furnish any kind of substantiation,” he said. item.title: ‘Elevate My Name’ – Detchawalit Hunts Contract-Clinching Win Against Yodkhunpon At The Inner Circle 40
item.description: Every young contender eventually meets his true measuring stick. For Detchawalit Silkmuaythai , it arrives in the form of a two-time K-1 Champion. Five straight wins have put a main roster deal in his sights, and a signature victory could seal it. That chance comes on Friday, November 27, when the 19-year-old meets Yodkhunpon “Piranha Muangthai” in the bantamweight Muay Thai main event of The Inner Circle 40 . The card goes down live in Asia primetime from Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium, exclusively for members at live.onefc.com . View this post on Instagram Before turning 19, the Silk Muaythai product tore through his first four ONE assignments without ever needing the judges, a feat many seasoned Thai stars never managed. Of the four men who tried, only Denis Dotsenko made it out of the opening round. That run set up a July meeting with French striker Tom “No Time” Casse at The Inner Circle 21 , who slowed the tempo and dragged him the full distance. Detchawalit adapted with a calculated three-round display, proving his poise runs deeper than youthful fire and moving his record to 51-5. For all he proved that night, the win still carried a bittersweet edge. Detchawalit told onefc.com: “He was really tough. No matter how hard I pressed, I couldn’t break him down. “I tried throwing every weapon I had, and it was the first time I couldn’t get a finish. It’s a little disappointing not to extend my finish streak.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship With his record still perfect inside ONE, the US$100,000 prize now glimmers at the end of the tunnel. Standing between him and that breakthrough, however, is a decorated veteran with 95 career wins. Facing such an accomplished countryman, Detchawalit intends to meet the occasion with everything he has. The gifted youngster said: “I was shocked. It was completely unexpected because I didn’t think I’d fight a Thai opponent yet, and his name carries much more weight. I didn’t think we’d cross paths this soon. “It’s a huge honor to fight him. I’ve never faced anyone with a name that big before.” View this post on Instagram Until now, Detchawalit’s ONE run has come entirely against international opposition. This time, he faces a rival who shares his roots and an instinctive feel for Muay Thai’s finer details. Over six demanding weeks, he has made certain his preparation matches the level he is about to face. He said: “I changed up my training a lot because his style is aggressive. He comes in fast with his punches and likes to brawl. He also has a heavy, dangerous left hook. “His weaknesses are probably being a bit slower than me and giving up height. I should be a step quicker with better speed, and I’ll use my speed and taller reach to my advantage.” Photo credit: ONE Championship Detchawalit Learns To Tame His Instincts Detchawalit Silkmuaythai sees this contest with rare clarity. item.title: ‘Aren’t going to win’- Spurs legend questions Luka Doncic’s ability to lead Lakers to NBA title
item.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images San Antonio Spurs legend Sean Elliott has dismissed the Los Angeles Lakers’ championship chances, insisting Luka Doncic and his teammates are not good enough to win the NBA title. Elliott, a 1999 NBA champion, questioned whether a team can build a championship-winning side around a player who dominates possession as much as Doncic. The comments come ahead of a major NBA Cup meeting between the Lakers and Spurs, who currently share identical records at the top of the Western Conference. Sean Elliott questions Los Angeles Lakers’ championship credentials ahead of San Antonio Spurs clash Speaking after San Antonio’s game against the Utah Jazz, Elliott made his feelings about the Lakers’ title chances clear. “Well, the Lakers aren’t gonna win the NBA championship. They’re not,” the Spurs colour commentator said. He acknowledged that Los Angeles have plenty of talent but questioned whether their current approach can deliver a championship. “I mean, they’ll be fun to watch,” he continued. “They have really good players. I like [Sandro Mamukelashvili] in a Laker uniform.” Elliott also highlighted Doncic’s defensive contributions as a concern, arguing that a team’s best player must be effective at both ends of the court. “Plus, your best player always, he’s gotta be a stalwart on the defensive end of the floor,” he said. “I firmly believe that.” His criticism also focused on Doncic’s usage rate, which currently stands at a league-leading 39 per cent. Elliott pointed out that no NBA champion has won the title with a player posting a usage rate above 35 per cent. However, the Lakers will have an opportunity to answer those doubts against the Spurs. Los Angeles are coming off a 109-94 victory over the Jazz, with Doncic scoring 28 points and adding eight assists. Walker Kessler also recorded 12 rebounds in the win. Kessler has already acknowledged San Antonio’s quality, praising Victor Wembanyama ahead of the matchup. “San Antonio is a very, very talented team,” he said via the LA Times’ Thuc Nhi Nguyen. ESPN Analytics gives the Spurs a 69 per cent chance of winning the NBA Cup Group C finale. The Lakers are also expected to have Austin Reaves available again after his injury. For Doncic and the Lakers, the meeting presents an opportunity to challenge Elliott’s assessment against one of the Western Conference’s strongest teams. item.title: Dortmund coach Kovac: We can hold our own against a strong opponent
item.description: Borussia Dortmund head coach Niko Kovac is pictured ahead of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium. (is associated with: «Dortmund coach Kovac: We can hold our own against a strong opponent») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Borussia Dortmund coach Nico Kovac praised his team for fighting back to rescue a point in the Champions League match against Arsenal on Tuesday evening. "It's a huge point for us, a huge moment for all of us - for the team and for the fans, who turned out in such big numbers today. In the end, of course, we're happy with the point," he said after the game. "We fought as a team, kept coming back, and showed that we can hold our own against a strong opponent." Arsenal took the lead in the 10th minute thanks to Viktor Gyökeres' goal, but Dortmund went back home with a point after Maximilian Beier levelled in the 55th. "In the locker room, we sat down and discussed what hadn't gone well in the first half. We wanted to come out with a different attitude," Beier said. "We really earned this. We battled hard at the end, and holding on to a one-one score here is far from an easy feat. We proved that we can compete with top-level teams." Dortmund now shift their attention back to the Bundesliga as they aim to remain top of the table after taking the lead from Bayern Munich last weekend. On Sunday, they welcome Bayer Leverkusen.
